headline.headline: SKUBAL HEADED TO DODGERS IN BLOCKBUSTER DEADLINE DEAL
headline.deck: Two-time Cy Young winner leaves Detroit in tears as Los Angeles adds ace to dynasty rotation
headline.body:
DETROIT — Tarik Skubal fought back tears Saturday night as he said goodbye to the only big-league organization he has ever known, confirming what sources across baseball had been reporting for hours: the two-time Cy Young Award winner is headed to Los Angeles in a blockbuster trade that reshapes the pennant race before Monday's deadline.

Skubal, who spent nine seasons in a Tigers uniform and carried the franchise through rebuilding years on the strength of a filthy fastball and arguably the best changeup in the American League, told reporters it was something he would never forget. The Dodgers, already back-to-back World Series champions, now add a proven October starter to a rotation that already ranked among the sport's best, giving Los Angeles a weapon that rivals across the NL West will spend the rest of the summer dreading.

For Detroit, the return package will define whether general manager Scott Harris extracted full market value for the crown jewel of the franchise. Trade analysts across the sport have given Los Angeles a clean A grade for the acquisition while the Tigers' grade remains in debate. Whatever Detroit received, the image of Skubal wiping his eyes at a Comerica Park podium will be the defining moment of the 2026 trade deadline.

secondary.headline: BLUE JAYS BLANK CARDINALS BEHIND SEVEN-INNING OUTBURST
secondary.deck: Toronto scores three in the seventh to pull away at Rogers Centre, 5-1
secondary.body:
TORONTO — The Toronto Blue Jays broke open a pitchers' duel Saturday with a three-run seventh inning and beat the visiting St. Louis Cardinals 5-1 before 41,819 fans at Rogers Centre. Toronto had scratched across single runs in the third and fourth innings to build a modest 2-0 lead before St. Louis answered with its only run of the afternoon in the sixth, but the Blue Jays answered immediately and decisively in the bottom of the seventh.

St. Louis starter Gastelum, who hit Giménez with a pitch during the contest, could not survive the late-inning damage as Toronto put the game away in two hours and 43 minutes. The Cardinals managed nothing in the final three innings against Toronto's bullpen, finishing the night with a single tally against a Blue Jays club that has now made late-inning offense a consistent weapon.

secondary.headline: DURANT SEES PHILLY AS NEXT DYNASTY AFTER LEBRON ADDITION
secondary.deck: Former champion compares new-look 76ers to his Golden State Warriors in offensive firepower
secondary.body:
Kevin Durant drew a striking comparison Saturday, telling reporters that the newly reconstructed Philadelphia 76ers remind him of the Golden State Warriors teams that won championships around him — and the reason is LeBron James. The 76ers added James in the offseason, assembling a collection of star offensive talent that Durant said matches the kind of firepower he experienced in his championship runs with Golden State.

The comments landed with weight given the source. Durant won two titles in Golden State alongside Stephen Curry and Klay Thompson, playing alongside perhaps the most potent offensive ensemble the league had seen in a generation. Whether Philadelphia can translate star power into a championship during these ongoing conference semifinals remains to be seen, but Durant's endorsement of the Sixers' ceiling gives the franchise a ringing endorsement from one of the game's all-time scorers.

secondary.headline: MARINERS WALK OFF TWINS ON MUNOZ'S WINNING PITCH IN NINTH
secondary.deck: Seattle survives Minnesota rally to take 4-3 win; Andres Munoz earns the decision
secondary.body:
SEATTLE — The Minnesota Twins chipped away inning by inning to tie the Seattle Mariners before a ninth-inning run sent 41,423 fans at T-Mobile Park home happy Saturday in a 4-3 Mariners victory. Seattle had jumped out to a 3-0 lead through two innings but the Twins answered with single runs in the fifth, sixth, and seventh to draw even, setting the stage for a decisive ninth that went Seattle's way with Andres Munoz earning the win.

Minnesota's comeback was methodical, with the Twins scratching across a run each inning over a three-frame stretch to erase what had looked like a comfortable Seattle cushion. An intentional walk issued to a Twins batter in the eighth inning showed the tension on both sides, but Seattle held and produced the winning run in the bottom of the ninth in a game that ran three hours and two minutes.

column.headline: DETROIT DESERVED BETTER THAN A TEARFUL GOODBYE
column.body:
There is something deeply uncomfortable about watching Tarik Skubal cry at a microphone while explaining what nine years in Detroit meant to him. The Tigers built that man into a two-time Cy Young winner, and the reward for their patience and his loyalty is that the Los Angeles Dodgers — already the most decorated team in recent baseball memory — get to add him to a rotation that didn't need the help. That is not sentiment talking. That is the structural problem at the heart of the sport.

The Dodgers will get an A for this deal. Every analyst in the country agrees. But the real grade being handed out Saturday night belongs to a sport that allows one franchise to function as a finishing school for talent that smaller-market clubs spend years developing. Skubal earned everything coming to him and deserves to pitch in October. The tears, though, belong to every Tigers fan who watched this one coming from miles away and could do nothing but wait.

story.headline: D-BACKS ERUPT FOR SEVEN IN SEVENTH, STUN GUARDIANS 12-8
story.deck: Arizona rallies from early deficit with massive seventh-inning explosion in Cleveland
story.body:
CLEVELAND — The Arizona Diamondbacks trailed by two runs and looked flat through six innings Saturday night, then sent 10 men to the plate in the seventh, scoring seven times to blow open a wild 12-8 victory over the Cleveland Guardians before 30,392 at Progressive Field. The Diamondbacks finished with 12 runs on the strength of home runs from Corbin Carroll, his 16th of the season, and Geraldo Perdomo, his ninth, while Nolan Arenado connected for his 15th to pace a lineup that left 25 runners on base.

Cleveland had jumped out to a 2-0 lead in the first inning and held that advantage through four frames before Arizona tied the game at 2 in the fifth. The Guardians appeared to stabilize, but the seventh inning unraveled their bullpen completely. The Diamondbacks sent run after run across the plate, turning a tight contest into a rout and handing reliever Aleman the victory. Cleveland mounted a five-run response in the eighth, cutting the deficit to 10-7, and Chase DeLauter hit his 12th home run of the year and Rhys Hoskins added his 12th as well, but the rally fell short.

The game featured four hit batsmen, including Kody Marte and Rocchio among those plunked, and took 3 hours and 39 minutes to complete. In other Saturday action, the Philadelphia Phillies shut out the Baltimore Orioles 5-0 behind a four-run eighth inning, Bryce Harper and Trea Turner each doubled, and four Phillies stole bases. The Houston Astros edged the Texas Rangers 5-4 as Yordan Alvarez reached base and Jeremy Peña recorded both a double and a triple, while Ranger Langford hit his 13th homer in a losing effort.

story.headline: WEMBANYAMA INKS NIKE SIGNATURE DEAL AS NBA OFFSEASON RESHAPES LEAGUE LANDSCAPE
story.deck: Spurs star joins sneaker royalty while Thunder, Warriors and 76ers all make offseason moves.
story.body:
San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama has signed a long-term deal with Nike that includes his own signature sneaker line, sources told ESPN Sunday, cementing the 22-year-old French phenom's status as the face of a new NBA generation. Wembanyama, who averaged 27.5 points and 11.7 rebounds per game last season while leading San Antonio back to playoff contention, becomes the latest global superstar to earn a Nike signature line, joining a pantheon that includes LeBron James and Kevin Durant. The deal is expected to be worth hundreds of millions over its lifetime and will feature a debut sneaker slated for release in the 2026-27 season.

In Oklahoma City, Chet Holmgren addressed reporters Saturday with a measured but candid acknowledgment that the Thunder's offseason roster turnover was simply an unavoidable reality of professional basketball. The Thunder, who reached the Western Conference Finals last spring, have lost multiple rotation contributors to free agency and trades in recent weeks. Holmgren, 24, insisted the core group remaining in OKC is hungry to push further into the postseason. Meanwhile in Golden State, the Warriors moved to shore up their depth by re-signing versatile forward Gary Payton II to a one-year, $3.9 million veteran minimum deal, reuniting the defensive specialist with a franchise where he thrived during their 2022 championship run.

Kevin Durant drew a striking historical parallel Saturday, comparing the newly constructed Philadelphia 76ers to his dynastic Golden State Warriors squads after Philly completed the addition of LeBron James to a roster already featuring Joel Embiid and a retooled supporting cast. Durant, speaking at a promotional event, noted that the 76ers now possess the kind of multi-threat offensive firepower that made his Warriors teams nearly impossible to game-plan against. League executives and scouts are already penciling Philadelphia in as an Eastern Conference title favorite, though questions about player health and roster chemistry will follow the 76ers deep into training camp when it opens in October.

story.headline: SHARKS LOCK UP GRAF, PENGUINS EXTEND NOVAK AS NHL OFFSEASON HEATS UP
story.deck: San Jose and Pittsburgh make moves while Russia faces continued ban from 2027 IIHF tournaments.
story.body:
San Jose locked up one of its most productive young forwards Sunday, re-signing Collin Graf to a three-year contract worth $12.75 million. Graf, who posted 21 goals and 25 assists across 81 games last season, gives the rebuilding Sharks a dependable offensive piece to build around as the franchise continues its climb back toward relevance in the Western Conference. The deal averages $4.25 million per season and keeps the 25-year-old in teal through the 2028-29 campaign.

In Pittsburgh, the Penguins moved to secure their own depth on Friday, signing forward Tommy Novak to a three-year contract extension. Novak has carved out a reputation as one of the more reliable two-way forwards in the league, and general manager Kyle Dubas wasted no time getting a deal done before the forward could test the open market. The move signals Pittsburgh's intent to remain competitive even as the organization navigates a transitional period following the retirement of franchise cornerstone Sidney Crosby.

Meanwhile, the IIHF confirmed Sunday that Russia will remain barred from four major international tournaments in 2027, extending the federation's firm stance following the invasion of Ukraine. Separately, Swedish Elite League club Farjestad BK rescinded its agreement with defenseman Cal Foote after a fierce backlash from supporters, leaving the blueliner scrambling to secure a landing spot heading into the fall.

story.headline: RECEIVERS MARKET HEATS UP AS TEAMS SCRAMBLE TO ADD WEAPONS THIS SPRING
story.deck: Several star wideouts changing addresses as NFL's passing game reshapes rosters
story.body:
The wide receiver carousel is spinning at full speed this May, with multiple Pro Bowl-caliber pass-catchers finding new homes as franchises look to upgrade their offenses heading into the 2026 campaign. The Dallas Cowboys made the boldest splash, agreeing to a three-year, $87 million deal with veteran slot receiver Tyler Lockett, who departed Seattle after a decade with the Seahawks. Meanwhile, the New England Patriots, armed with fresh cap space and a young quarterback to develop, signed DeAndre Hopkins to a one-year prove-it deal worth $14 million, reuniting the 33-year-old with offensive coordinator Alex Van Pelt.

The draft class analysis continues to dominate front-office conversations as teams digest what they landed in late April. The Cleveland Browns, who selected Louisville quarterback Tyler Shough with the fourth overall pick, watched their new signal-caller earn strong reviews during last week's rookie minicamp at the team's Berea facility. Scouts around the league noted Shough's quick release and command of the huddle as particular strengths, though his ability to handle pressure situations in the AFC North remains the defining question surrounding the franchise's latest rebuilding effort.

On the trade front, the Las Vegas Raiders sent disgruntled cornerback Nate Hobbs to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a second-round pick in 2027, ending a prolonged contract standoff that had poisoned the Raiders' locker room atmosphere for months. Vikings general manager Kwesi Adofo-Mensah called Hobbs a cornerstone piece for a secondary that surrendered too many big plays during last season's disappointing 8-9 finish. Raiders head coach Pete Carroll, now in his second year with the club, told reporters the move allowed the organization to move forward without distraction as voluntary workouts intensify through May.
